title: Core Monetization Models Explained
description: Learn to identify and distinguish the five major monetization models used by today's leading companies.

interactions.prompt: Which monetization model does Netflix primarily use?

options.text: Freemium with ad-supported tier
Subscription with recurring monthly or annual fees
Usage-based charging per movie watched
Marketplace connecting content creators and viewers

interactions.teachingPreamble: A subscription model charges customers a recurring fee—monthly or annually—for continuous access to a product or service. Netflix charges ~$15/month for unlimited streaming, generating predictable recurring revenue that now exceeds $33 billion annually. The key advantage is revenue predictability, which makes forecasting and investment planning much easier.

interactions.prompt: Spotify reports: 615M total users, 239M paying subscribers, $13.2B revenue. Free users generate $1.5B from ads. What's the most important signal about their monetization?

options.text: Most users are free, so ads drive the business
Paid subscribers are under 40% but generate ~89% of revenue
Total user count is the key growth metric
Ad revenue is growing faster than subscriptions

chartData.title: Spotify Revenue per User by Segment

interactions.prompt: What is the primary business goal of offering a free tier in a freemium model?

options.text: Maximizing ad revenue from free users
Reducing customer support costs significantly
Acquiring users cheaply then converting them to paid
Competing on price with open-source alternatives

interactions.teachingPreamble: The freemium model gives users a basic product for free while charging for premium features. Dropbox famously grew to 700M users by offering 2GB free storage, then converting ~4% to paid plans starting at $12/month. The free tier acts as a massive acquisition funnel—lowering the barrier to try your product so you can demonstrate value before asking for payment.

interactions.prompt: In a ____ model, customers pay based on how much they consume, like AWS charging per compute hour or Twilio charging per API call.

options.text: Subscription
Freemium
Usage-based
Marketplace

interactions.prompt: You're launching a B2B analytics tool for SMBs. Usage varies wildly—some clients run 10 reports/month, others run 10,000. Which model best balances fairness, simplicity, and revenue?

options.text: Pure usage-based: charge per report generated
Flat subscription: one price for unlimited reports
Tiered subscription: plans with report volume ranges
Freemium: free up to 50 reports, then pay per report

interactions.prompt: What makes a marketplace model fundamentally different from the other monetization models?

options.text: It always requires a subscription fee from buyers
The company creates value by connecting buyers and sellers
Revenue comes only from advertising to users
It eliminates the need for customer acquisition

interactions.teachingPreamble: A marketplace model generates revenue by facilitating transactions between two or more parties, typically taking a commission or fee per transaction. Airbnb charges hosts a 3% fee and guests up to 14.2%, earning $9.9B in 2023 revenue without owning a single property. The challenge is the 'chicken-and-egg' problem: you need both supply and demand to create value.

interactions.prompt: Rank these monetization models from MOST to LEAST predictable monthly revenue for the business: (a) Usage-based like AWS, (b) Annual subscription like Salesforce, (c) Marketplace commission like Uber, (d) Freemium like Slack.

options.text: Usage-based (AWS)
Annual subscription (Salesforce)
Marketplace commission (Uber)
Freemium (Slack)

interactions.prompt: Your SaaS analytics tool with tiered subscriptions just lost 30% of enterprise clients to a competitor offering pure usage-based pricing. Remaining clients say your mid-tier feels too expensive for light months. What's your best move?

options.text: Switch entirely to usage-based pricing immediately
Add a hybrid model: base subscription plus usage overages
Lower all tier prices by 30% to retain customers
Offer a freemium tier to attract new small customers

interactions.priorContext: Earlier you chose tiered subscriptions for your B2B analytics tool. Now enterprise clients are leaving because rigid tiers don't match their variable usage patterns, forcing you to reconsider your monetization approach.
